title: Regulatory Notice: DosaTech ScreenBridge Compromise — MDWS-FE-2026

fields.office: Central District, Drinking Water and Groundwater Division
fields.subject: Submission of Forensic Evidence — DosaTech ScreenBridge Compromise (MDWS-FE-2026)
fields.applicability: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer, all personnel involved in cyber-incident response and regulatory reporting
fields.authority: Ohio Revised Code § 3745.01; 40 CFR 141.71 (Federal Emergency Response)
fields.purpose:
The City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer has submitted forensic evidence confirming a cyber-physical compromise of the caustic feed control system (NAOH-FC-203) via an unauthorized DosaTech ScreenBridge agent on MBW-HMI-02 (10.72.10.22). The attacker used a fake vendor identity and bypassed multi-factor authentication to increase the setpoint to 38 mg/L without triggering HMI alarms or field safety devices. The attack remains under investigation by CISA and the FBI. This directive confirms the submission of evidence for attribution and forensic analysis.

The incident is classified as a Level 3 — Public Health Emergency under ERP Section 4.4. All actions taken to isolate, monitor, and restore the system are to be documented and reported via the DDAGW-ELR-2026 portal within 24 hours of verification.
actions: Submit the forensic evidence package (SEC-4 form, MBW-HMI-02 forensic image, DosaTech session audit log) to CISA via the WaterISAC portal within 2 hours of receipt.
Notify the FBI Cyber Task Force via the WaterISAC portal and request a joint attribution and forensic review under Section 12.3 (External Reporting Clocks).
Confirm receipt and next steps from CISA and FBI via WaterISAC within 4 hours of submission.
Maintain the Do Not Drink advisory for Zone 1 until two clean sample rounds (pH ≤ 9.0, caustic ≤ 15 mg/L) are confirmed and verified by DDAGW.
Report final lab verification to the Ohio EPA DDAGW within 1 hour of confirmation.
